sections.h2: Which offices handle your tax bill
sections.html:
Everything runs through the Redwood County Government Center at 403 South Mill Street in Redwood Falls. Valuation and classification belong to the Assessor, reached at 507-637-4008. Billing and collection belong to the Auditor-Treasurer at 507-637-4013. The Recorder files deeds at 507-637-4032.

Letters go to P.O. Box 130, Redwood Falls, MN 56283. Phone lines at the assessor's desk stay open weekdays until 4:30 p.m.

Redwood County is rolling cropland in southwest Minnesota, and Redwood Falls is the county seat. Population is 15,265, which is 1.0% fewer than the 2020 base count. A typical owner-occupied house is valued at $158,200. Owners live in 78.4% of homes, and renters pay a median of $757 a month. There are 7,133 housing units, and only seven building permits were issued in 2025.

The 2020 census counted 10.8% of housing units vacant and 21.4% of occupied homes rented. At these prices, even a modest balance of back tax or penalty is a real line item on a closing statement.

Real estate tax comes due in mid-May and mid-October. Agricultural land and manufactured homes owe the second half in mid-November, and in 2026 that date is Monday, November 16.

Late payment penalties come from Minnesota Statutes section 279.01 and differ for homestead and nonhomestead land. The county also bills $30 for any bounced check, failed electronic payment or reversed payment.

sections.h2: What payment options does the Auditor-Treasurer offer?
sections.html:
The county has an online payments page with a tax parcel lookup, and the Government Center accepts payments over the counter or through the post. A Direct Payment Plan pulls the amount from your checking or savings account, either twice a year or in one annual draft. Call 507-637-4013 to enroll.

Escrow customers should still read the statement. Before closing, request a payoff figure for the parcel from the same office, which also publishes the yearly delinquent tax list and notices of forfeited property sales and sales with unclaimed surplus.

sections.h2: How the assessor arrives at your value
sections.html:
Every parcel gets a classification based on how it is used and an estimated market value fixed as of January 2. Appraisers walk each property on a five year cycle under Minnesota Statutes section 273.01, and tax-exempt parcels on a six year cycle. A new addition can bring an earlier visit.

The annual notice in spring shows that value and class, and it sets the tax for the following year. Details that affect homestead treatment:

  • On January 2 or December 1, the owner or a qualifying relative has to be living there.
  • The application deadline is December 31 of the assessment year, filed with the Assessor.
  • People who are blind or permanently disabled may apply for a separate class.
  • The disabled veterans' homestead exclusion form and special agricultural homestead forms come from the Assessor's office.

Start by phoning the assessor about the notice. Failing that, the next stop is the local board of appeal and equalization for your city or township. The Assessor's office hosts those meetings each April. In most cases you must be heard locally before your case can reach the county board, which meets in June in the Commissioner's Room.

Bring evidence that points to a specific parcel, such as a recent sale of a similar house or photos of a defect. Beyond the boards, a petition to district court or Tax Court under section 278.01 is the last route, and it has an April 30 filing date.

sections.h2: What if tax is unpaid when you sell?
sections.html:
Tax still open in early January turns delinquent under section 279.02, with an extra 2% added right away. The tax matters at closing for a second reason: the auditor must mark a deed with a no-delinquent-tax note before the Recorder accepts it under section 272.12. Probate distribution deeds and transfer on death deeds are among the listed exceptions.

In practice the title agent subtracts what you owe from your proceeds, so a quick call to the Auditor-Treasurer keeps surprises out of the closing statement. A cash sale follows the same rule, though it skips any lender escrow payoff.

sections.h2: Recording tools to use before a sale
sections.html:
The Recorder offers three. LandShark is a web tool for searching land records and viewing document images, and an account needs a signed web portal agreement with an original wet signature plus a set-up fee. Land Notification emails you when anything is filed against your personal or business name, so a surprise lien shows up quickly. The eCRV tool is where the sale certificate gets filed, and paper certificates have not been accepted for sales since October 1, 2014.

After closing, the assessor drops homestead classification on the sold property for the next assessment year unless the buyer applies and qualifies, under section 272.115.

faqs.q: What is the last Redwood County tax deadline of the year?
faqs.a: The second half on agricultural property and manufactured homes, due mid-November. In 2026 that date is Monday, November 16. Standard real estate second halves come due October 15.

faqs.q: Who can I call about a Redwood County home value I think is too high?
faqs.a: Call the County Assessor at 507-637-4008. If the answer does not satisfy you, the next steps are the local board in April and the county board in June.

faqs.q: Can a Redwood County house be sold with property tax still owing?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance has to be cleared before the Recorder will file the deed, and it normally comes out of the seller's proceeds. Ask the Auditor-Treasurer at 507-637-4013 for the exact payoff.

faqs.q: What is the Redwood County homestead application deadline?
faqs.a: December 31 of the assessment year. The home must be owned and occupied by the owner or a qualifying relative as of January 2 or December 1.

faqs.q: Will the buyer automatically get my Redwood County homestead status?
faqs.a: No. After a transfer the assessor removes homestead for the following assessment year unless the new owner files an application and qualifies.
